title: Layer 2 round 1 major SE+DE: remote-tracking ref stripping hardcodes origin against the declared remote-name-generic rule
description: refs.rs:46 strips only literal 'origin', but the doc and dispatch-data's adopted rule say 'the remote name stripped' generically; a remote named upstream/fork leaves upstream/feature/x unstripped -> reported off-grammar (standing false positive), and a local branch literally named origin/x is mangled. Disposition: list refs/heads and refs/remotes separately, strip exactly one remote segment for remote refs only. Owner: software-engineer. Validator: data-engineer.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: Fixed in d84109f5: the ref listing runs as two for-each-ref queries — refs/heads short, refs/remotes full — feeding pub normalize_ref_lines, pure and tested: the remote segment strips structurally for any remote name (upstream included, origin no longer hardcoded), each remote's symbolic HEAD skips, dedup preserves order locals-first, and a local branch literally named origin/x survives intact.
